sources.title: Deterministic and Reliable Software-Defined Vehicles: key building blocks, challenges, and vision
sources.role: Author paper/preprint used to verify the reported architecture, method/evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The paper surveys deterministic SDV development around service-oriented architectures, virtualization, and deterministic intra- and inter-vehicle communications.

The authors describe SDV compute as moving from many distributed ECUs toward more centralized computing combined with zone-based architecture, while emphasizing deterministic network and compute guarantees for critical services.
claims.context: Literature synthesis and author framing, not an independent fleet measurement.

claims.text: The proposed vision architecture contains five coordinating elements: deterministic network configurator, data-layer configurator, hypervisor configurator, vehicle abstraction layer, and software orchestrator.
claims.context: Proposed vision rather than deployed production architecture.

limitations.text: The five-component architecture is a survey-derived vision; the paper discusses validation paths rather than establishing production deployment or end-to-end certification of the complete architecture.
Many architecture-transition statements synthesize cited literature and industry material and should not be treated as independently measured facts from this paper.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Deterministic and Reliable Software-Defined Vehicles: key building blocks, challenges, and vision; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The v2 primary paper verifies the survey scope, centralized/zonal SDV framing, deterministic service requirements, and the five-part vision architecture; these remain literature synthesis/author proposals rather than empirical production validation.

editorial.why_now_note: It connects compute centralization, zonal topology, SOA, virtualization and deterministic networking into one coherent architectural responsibility model during the survey window.
editorial.rationale: Useful synthesis/vision evidence for architecture framing, with clear separation between surveyed facts and the authors' proposed orchestration architecture.
